title: Same Leaves Left to Right
statement:
You get the roots of two non-empty binary trees, a and b. A leaf is a node with no children. Reading a tree's leaves from left to right gives its leaf sequence.

Return true if the two trees have exactly the same leaf sequence, same values in the same order, and false otherwise. The trees may have completely different shapes and inner values.

examples.why: Both leaf sequences are 1, 3, 7, even though the shapes and inner nodes differ.
The sequences are 2, 3 and 3, 2. Same leaves, wrong order.
a's leaves are 7, 7 and b's single leaf is 7. Comparing sets of leaf values would wrongly say true.

constraints: Each tree has between 1 and 200 nodes
hints: You need each tree's leaves in left-to-right order. Which traversal visits them in that order?
Any depth-first traversal that goes left before right meets the leaves left to right. Collect a node's value when it has no children.
Collect both sequences into lists and compare them element by element, including their lengths.

explain.intuition:
Inner nodes and shape do not matter; only the leaves and their order do. A depth-first walk that always handles the left child before the right one reaches leaves in exactly left-to-right order, the same order in which a DOM walk would visit text nodes on a line.

So collect each tree's leaf values into a list and compare the two lists. The comparison must be exact: same length, same values, same order. A set or a sorted copy loses either the order or the duplicates.
steps: Write collect(node, out): if the node has no children, push its value; otherwise recurse into the left child, then the right child.
Collect the leaves of a and of b.
Return whether the two lists have equal length and equal elements at every position.
pitfalls: Comparing sets or sorted lists of leaves. Order and repeated values both matter.
Treating a node with one child as a leaf. A leaf has no children at all.
Comparing only up to the shorter list's length, so a sequence that is a prefix of the other looks equal.

complexity.space: O(n + m) for the lists and recursion

solutions.title: Collect both leaf lists
solutions.idea: A left-first DFS collects each tree's leaves in order; then compare the lists.

solutions.title: Walk both trees in lockstep
solutions.idea: Two explicit stacks yield the next leaf of each tree on demand. Compare leaf by leaf and stop at the first difference, without storing whole sequences.

followups: Write it with generators (function* in JS, yield in Python) so each tree produces leaves lazily.
Compare the leaf sequences of k trees at once. How do you report which trees differ?
